headline: STI fell 0.6% to 4,930.83 on Wednesday as the chip sell-off spread; banks slipped, REITs and Singtel rose. Overnight the US proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies, Singapore up to 20% (semis, pharma exempt, not before late Jan). Hot US PCE keeps a Dec Fed hike priced. US shut Thursday.

sectors.why: No sector-wide news. HRnetGroup rose about 2% on Wednesday after nine-month revenue grew 12% on semiconductor hiring, but one result does not set a direction.
Singtel was the STI's top gainer (+1.9%) as money moved out of chip stocks into defensives. That can continue while tech is volatile, but there is no new telco news.
No sector-specific news; the proposed US tariffs could weigh on exporters of goods to the US, but details per product are not yet clear.
No sector-specific news; Singapore core inflation eased to 1.5% in October, which keeps cost pressure low.
No sector-specific news; the broad market mood is cautious after two weak sessions.
No sector-specific news; US tariff talk is a mild risk for trade-linked distributors over the coming months.

The AI chip sell-off continues: the US chip index fell almost 8% on Tuesday and chip stocks fell again on Wednesday; AEM dropped 6.8%. Semiconductors are exempt from the new tariff plan, which limits the extra damage.
US crude rose about 2.5% and energy led US gains on Wednesday, ending the recent slide; one day is not enough to call a month-long trend.
DBS (-1.2%), OCBC and UOB fell while the REIT index rose 0.6%. US yields eased, which helps REITs, but a December Fed hike is still fully priced after hot October PCE inflation.
No sector-specific news.
No sector-specific news; patented pharmaceuticals are excluded from the proposed US tariffs.
BRC Asia jumped 4.9% after FY profit rose 22%, and Singapore's strong growth (around 6% this year) supports building activity, but Seatrium fell 4.2% after announcing retrenchments.
No sector-specific news.

The US proposed a Section 301 tariff of up to 20% on Singapore goods (10% with a trade deal). Machinery and equipment makers are not in the exempt groups, so this is a headwind, though nothing takes effect before late January.
No sector-specific news; low local inflation is a mild support.
